findings.statement: game reading: o building an open stack up column b, unanswered by x on the diagonal through b5, is bad for x
findings.check: L4 reading against the L3 grid
findings.evidence: a domain-level rule (who holds the crossing at b5: on iff x's count >= o's) confirmed exactly on every training row and the 3x3 grid; the 3040 rows it switches off on have an x-win rate of 56.2% vs 66.4%. Meaningful

xDiagD6G3Gate.why: The reading ('an x piece on d6-g3 removes a small bonus') is relu(0.0138 - 1.47 z) x 0.043 in words, scored 1.0 with the input itself as the concept; no game reason is given or found.

xB5E2vsOB3B6Gate.why: A game-level rule about who holds the crossing cell b5 (on iff x's open count on b5-e2 >= o's on b3-b6) that the model confirms on every training row and on the full 3x3 count grid, with the off rows a weaker group for x (56.2% vs 66.4%).

xThrEvenUnit.why: An always-on ReLU of one input (on for 54045 of 54045 rows) that partly cancels the input's direct term; the hypothesis itself says 'described, not explained'.

xLinesDirect.why: The 0.80 concept is the formula's own sign pattern over its 35 connected lines; the reading stated in board terms alone (low rows and the centre column, minus lines touching row six) scores only r2 0.356, and the negative lines are explained as within-model offsets, not play.

oLinesDirect.why: The reading in board terms alone (o horizontals on rows two to four and the two diagonals, minus the centre verticals) scores r2 0.767, so it is more than the sign pattern, but row four is mixed inside the part (b4-e4 +0.148, c4-f4 +0.041 against a4-d4 -0.380) and the centre-vertical discount is an offset without a game reading.

aggregatesDirect.why: Open-line material x minus o plus centre presence and an o even-row threat penalty is a game reading the model confirms in direction, but the stated equal worth of open twos and singles holds only per sd (per line a two is worth about three singles: 49.2 -> 62.2% vs 49.2 -> 53.8%; a game-unit count scores 0.946 vs 0.817) and 'nearly decisive' overstates a 23% mean predicted chance on the real rows.
